ross-parry-229.title: Canoe of the Savage Islands, Hudson's Strait
ross-parry-229.description: A kayaker paddles among loose ice off the Savage Islands in Hudson Strait, with other boats and a group of figures beyond. The volume's binder's list gives the plate its title, and George Francis Lyon, who drew it, met the people of these islands as the Fury and Hecla worked west in July 1821; Edward Finden engraved it for William Edward Parry's published journal.

ross-parry-230.title: Cutting into Winter Island, October, 1821
ross-parry-230.description: The Fury and the Hecla lie at the head of a canal sawn through the new ice, with parties of men walking out along it carrying ice-saws and a dark lane of open water curving across the foreground. George Francis Lyon drew the scene and William Edward Parry described the work in his journal; it is the second of the three winterings in which both captains cut their ships into a harbour by hand.

ross-parry-231.title: Interior of an Esquimaux Snow-hut, Winter Island, 1822
ross-parry-231.description: The inside of an Iglulingmiut snow house at Winter Island: the domed roof of cut blocks overhead, a woman seated on the sleeping platform with a bowl, meat and skins hung about her, a stone lamp burning and a long pole across the room. George Francis Lyon drew the interior during the winter of 1821-22, and William Edward Parry's account of the same houses -- the arch of blocks carrying its own weight, the window of clear ice in each roof -- runs alongside it in the journal.

ross-parry-236.title: Sledges of the Esquimaux
ross-parry-236.description: A fan-hitched team draws a loaded Iglulingmiut sledge with its driver, seen in profile against open snow. George Francis Lyon drew it, and William Edward Parry's journal sets out the measurements of the sledge, the harness and the fan hitch in detail; the ships' officers timed such a team over two miles in five-and-twenty minutes.

ross-parry-237.title: Esquimaux House built of ice
ross-parry-237.description: A house built of clear ice slabs stands on the snow, its faceted walls catching the light, with a man in fur dress, a harnessed dog, a second dog and a sledge with coiled line in front of it. George Francis Lyon drew the building for William Edward Parry's journal; it is one of the few contemporary images of an ice house as distinct from a snow house.

ross-parry-238.title: Groupe of Esquimaux at Igloolik, 1823
ross-parry-238.description: A man and a woman in heavy winter dress stand with a small child beside them while other figures, a dog team and a sledge cross the snow behind. George Francis Lyon drew the group at Igloolik during the second wintering, one of the studies of Iglulingmiut clothing he made for William Edward Parry's journal.

ross-parry-239.title: Nakahu and his Wife Oomna
ross-parry-239.description: A double portrait of two named people of Igloolik: Nakahu standing in caribou-skin clothing with a long spear, and his wife Oomna beside him. George Francis Lyon drew them during the wintering of 1822-23; Edward Finden's separate engraving of Oomna alone was published from the same sitting.

ross-parry-240.title: Esquimaux building a Snow-hut
ross-parry-240.description: Snow houses and a raised meat-drying rack stand on the sea ice with dogs and fur-clad figures among them, one of them at work cutting and setting blocks. George Francis Lyon drew the scene near Igloolik, and William Edward Parry's journal describes the same construction: each block cut to the shape the arch requires, so that the dome carries itself.

ross-parry-241.title: Esquimaux killing Deer in a Lake
ross-parry-241.description: Iglulingmiut hunters, several of them in kayaks, spear caribou swimming a lake, with a camp of skin tents on the shore beyond. George Francis Lyon drew the summer hunt near Igloolik for William Edward Parry's journal; Parry noted that Toolooak's mother wore a girdle strung with twenty-nine caribou ears taken by her son in a single season.

ross-parry-232.description: Two large animals hauled out on shore ice, drawn by George Francis Lyon for William Edward Parry's journal. This is one of four plates of the seal and walrus hunt bound between pages 171 and 176; their engraved captions are illegible in this copy, so the plate is described from what it shows rather than from its printed title.

ross-parry-233.description: A hunter lies among ice hummocks with a harpoon and line laid ready while other figures wait at the water's edge -- the patient still-hunting at breathing-holes that supplied much of the Iglulingmiut winter diet, as George Francis Lyon and William Edward Parry both described it. One of four plates of the seal and walrus hunt bound between pages 171 and 176, described from what it shows because the engraved caption is illegible in this copy.

ross-parry-234.description: A single hunter crouches behind a low wall of snow beside a seal's breathing-hole, his spear laid on the ice. Drawn by George Francis Lyon for William Edward Parry's journal; one of four plates of the seal and walrus hunt bound between pages 171 and 176, described from what it shows because the engraved caption is illegible in this copy.

ross-parry-235.description: A hunter stoops over a struck animal holding the line, while a second stands off with a harpoon and others watch from further out on the ice. Drawn by George Francis Lyon for William Edward Parry's journal; one of four plates of the seal and walrus hunt bound between pages 171 and 176, described from what it shows because the engraved caption is illegible in this copy.
